pool.text: Joslyn Art Museum opened with large art collections.
The Star was founded in North Omaha as Nebraska's only African-American newspaper.
Strategic Air Command relocated to the Omaha suburb, providing a major economic boost.
Omaha's Union Stockyards overtook Chicago's stockyards as the United States' meat packing center.
Woodmen Tower was completed and became Omaha's tallest building and first major skyscraper.
First Data Corporation was founded in Omaha as a large credit-card processor.
A major tornado and a major blizzard caused more than $100 million in damages.
Omaha Children's Museum was established as a place where children can learn through play.
The Bemis Center for Contemporary Arts was founded as an urban artist colony.
Level 3 Communications was founded in Omaha as Kiewit Diversified Group.
The demolition of Jobber's Canyon led to the creation of the ConAgra Foods campus.
Warren Buffett purchased UUNET, one of the largest Internet backbones in the world, for $2 billion.
The First National Bank Tower on Dodge Street was completed as the tallest building.
The Nebraska Legislature approved a plan to create a learning community for Omaha-area school districts.
The Bob Kerrey Pedestrian Bridge was opened to foot and bicycle traffic.
Nebraska lawmakers moved Offutt Air Force Base and Bellevue out of the Omaha-based 2nd district.
Douglas County treasurer John Ewing was elected mayor, ending Stothert's administration.
The Mutual of Omaha Headquarters Tower will be the new tallest building upon completion.
